study: UK House of Commons 2024 election official constituency-level results
unit: UK constituency; up to 650, 4 nations and English regions
prespecified_exclusions: Only missing electorate/turnout or no winner-runner candidate votes for computation; report exclusions and special Speaker/NI observations; don't discard by result
classification: All cycles exploratory until independently replicated; contemporaneous margins and vote shares are post-election, cannot be used in genuine pre-election prediction.
A: Does the final winner margin and ENP offer practical explanatory power for constituency turnout beyond a nation/region-only mean, when held-out geographic regions are evaluated without tuning?

B.H1: Region-only/UK baseline is competitive; margin+fragmentation cannot reduce MAE >= 0.5 percentage points in held-out geography
B.H0: Joint model improves heldout-geography MAE by >= 0.5 pp
B.Halt: The region model cannot predict unseen region fixed effects and requires careful baseline.

C: Choose deterministic leave-one-nation-out or grouped region CV (not random row split); baselines training mean, turnout~margin, turnout~margin+ENP, region model only when test group seen; report MAE/RMSE, residual by nation, and acknowledge all explanatory variables computed after voting, so not genuine forecast.
F: 4 nation holdouts not enough to quantify country-general model; NI distinct electoral system, no prospective claim.
G: Internal same-election crossvalidation not independent future replication.
J: Keep negative results and close only after actual execution.
